summary.master_summary:
# chat + announcing my final project

## ⚡ Quick Stream Highlights (TL;DR)
- Gawr Gura expresses profound relief and peace regarding her public departure, thanking her community for their understanding and support.
- She teases an upcoming room review collaboration with Nanashi Mumei.
- The main reveal is her 'beautifully heartbreaking' final project: an original song titled 'Ash' with a fully animated music video.
- The song, 'Ash,' was a year-long project co-written with Casey Edwards (DMC5 composer) and animated by Ma (Myth Bad End animator), described by Gawr Gura as 'a piece of my soul'.
- Gawr Gura shared lighthearted future plans, including playing 'Mortuary's Assistant' and potentially returning to school for math.

## ⭐ Standout Stories & Timestamps
- **[⏱️ 00:02:45](#t=00:02:45) Company Departure Acknowledgement**: Gawr Gura directly thanks viewers for their understanding and insane support regarding her decision to leave the company.
- **[⏱️ 00:15:37](#t=00:15:37) Relief of Public Departure**: Gawr Gura shares the immense relief she feels now that her departure is public, describing the difficulty of maintaining a facade before the announcement.
- **[⏱️ 00:31:36](#t=00:31:36) Casey Edwards Collaboration Revealed**: Gawr Gura excitedly reveals her new original song was co-written and produced by Casey Edwards, known for his work on Devil May Cry 5.
- **[⏱️ 00:32:30](#t=00:32:30) Ma's Animation & Dream Team**: Gawr Gura announces that Ma, who animated the Hololive Myth Bad End video, created the fully animated music video for her new song, calling them her 'dream team'.
- **[⏱️ 00:39:21](#t=00:39:21) Emotional Impact of Song Creation**: Gawr Gura praises Casey Edwards for taking her 'trauma dumping' and transforming it into a deeply meaningful piece of music she will cherish forever.
- **[⏱️ 00:43:08](#t=00:43:08) Song Title Reveal: 'Ash'**: After much anticipation and teasing, Gawr Gura finally reveals the title of her new original song and animated music video: 'Ash'.

## ⏱️ Timeline Breakdown
- **[⏱️ 00:00:36](#t=00:00:36)**: Gawr Gura expresses initial awkwardness after her major announcement, thanks Nanashi Mumei for an upcoming room review, and acknowledges fan support for her departure. She teases a 'beautifully heartbreaking' final project, discusses compiling unreleased clips, and addresses member content and VOD comment status.
- **[⏱️ 00:15:03](#t=00:15:03)**: Gawr Gura reflects on the immense relief of her departure becoming public, discusses post-departure plans including Rust collaborations and a farewell karaoke. She humorously counts down her remaining time, shares personal plans, expresses a fear of volcanoes, and briefly mentions the long-awaited 'final project'.
- **[⏱️ 00:30:02](#t=00:30:02)**: Gawr Gura, emotional, announces her new original song and animated music video, 'Ash.' She reveals collaborations with Casey Edwards (co-writer) and Ma (animator), highlighting the project's year-long development and profound emotional impact. She describes the song as 'a piece of my soul' for her fans.
- **[⏱️ 00:45:01](#t=00:45:01)**: Gawr Gura, in a state of hurried excitement, directs her audience to her newly released song and animated music video, apologizing for not setting up a premiere. She acknowledges her flustered state due to the release, thanks her viewers, and promises a more composed return for a detailed discussion.

chunks.summary: The VTuber opens the stream expressing initial awkwardness and uncertainty following a major announcement (her decision to leave the company). She quickly transitions to positive news, thanking Nanashi Mumei and announcing an upcoming room review collaboration with her. She fondly recalls a previous hilarious room review with Nanashi Mumei, involving a bunk bed and uncontrollable laughter, and states the next one is scheduled for 'tomorrow'. The VTuber then explicitly thanks her viewers for their 'insane support' and understanding regarding her decision to leave the company, apologizing to anyone who might be unhappy but expressing optimism for the future. She humorously hints at 'a shark loose on the internet,' a clear reference to Gawr Gura. She then reveals that a 'beautifully heartbreaking' final project will be announced at the half-hour mark, describing herself as a 'one-man show' and 'the entire circus' due to her current scattered mental state. She shares an idea to compile years of unreleased clips and bloopers from her PC into a video, mentioning a clip featuring all the 'Myth girls.' The conversation then shifts to her feeling unwell with a 'tummy ache,' attributing it to anxiety about the stream. She addresses the future of member content, stating she is unsure, but confirms that regular VODs will remain available with comments frozen and locked due to moderation reasons. She playfully confuses Star Wars' 'carbonite' with uranium and jokes about only having seen the first Star Wars movie.

chunks.summary: In this segment, the speaker reflects on their upcoming departure, expressing a profound sense of relief and peace now that the news is public. They describe the difficulty of knowing about their own and others' departures for a long time, having to maintain a facade that everything was 'okay' when it wasn't, feeling the 'weight' lifted off their shoulders once they no longer had to hide it. Looking ahead, the speaker discusses their post-departure plans, including a desire to collaborate with other members, specifically mentioning Rust despite acknowledging it as a major time sink that could derail other tasks. They ponder the limited time remaining, humorously counting down their last '128 hours.' Other plans include a farewell karaoke stream featuring favorite songs and ukulele, and personal activities like eating strawberries, crying, and leaning on friends. They joke about opening a bakery but doubt the quality of their products. The speaker also muses on potential post-career paths such as going back to school for math and dreams of a vacation, listing various travel destinations like the Grand Canyon or mountains, while explicitly stating a fear of volcanoes. The segment concludes with them expressing a strong desire to play the horror game 'Mortuary's Assistant,' clarifying it's unrelated to their departure, and sharing a fond memory of building a 'Pepe' sign with a neighbor in HoloRust, before briefly mentioning a 'final project' that has been a long time in the making.

highlights.description: The speaker shares the immense relief they feel now that their departure is public, contrasting it with the long, difficult period of knowing and having to pretend everything was fine while others also left.
The speaker metaphorically describes the sense of relief as 'the elephant in the room that only I could see was no longer in the room' after their departure was announced.
The speaker humorously identifies Rust as their 'kryptonite' and 'Hololive live rust,' acknowledging that if they start playing it, they won't get anything else done before their departure.
The speaker jokingly calculates how many days 128 hours is and frames it as a countdown to their 'self-destruct,' with 'Your time begins now.'
The speaker shares immediate post-graduation plans: eating a lot of strawberries, crying a lot, and leaning heavily on their friends.
While discussing vacation spots and wanting to see mountains, the speaker explicitly states, 'Volcanoes. No thank you. Oh, no thank you. I'm scared of volcanoes.'
The speaker expresses a strong, unrelated desire to play 'Mortuary's Assistant' before graduating, clarifying it's just because they enjoy the game and not tied to their departure.
The speaker fondly recalls a favorite HoloRust moment where they were neighbors with 'PCOS and B,' and they exchanged signs, with the speaker drawing 'Pe' and the neighbor completing it.
The speaker briefly mentions a 'final project' that has been a long time coming and was initially something they doubted would ever be approved, but it ultimately happened.

chunks.summary: Gawr Gura, visibly emotional and fighting back tears, announces the release of her new original song and fully animated music video. She expresses immense pride and joy over the project, calling the collaborators her 'dream team'. She reveals that the song was co-written and produced by Casey Edwards, known for his work on Devil May Cry 5's soundtrack, and the music video was animated by Ma, who previously animated the Hololive Myth Bad End video. Gura shares that the project has been in development for over a year, possibly two, and was an emotionally challenging experience to create, often leading her to cry during recording and meetings. She praises Casey Edwards for taking her 'trauma dumping' and transforming it into a deeply meaningful piece of music. Gura thanks her fanbase for their continuous support, stating she wouldn't have been able to create the song without them. After some playful hesitation and struggling with the technical aspects of scheduling, she reveals the song's title, 'Ash,' and decides to make it public immediately.

highlights.description: Gura begins the segment by reassuring chat she's not going to cry, despite her emotional state, as she prepares to announce something big.
Overwhelmed with emotion, Gura humorously asks for help: 'Somebody help her. Somebody get online and help this shark.'
Gura excitedly reveals she collaborated with Casey Edwards, known for 'Bury the Light' and 'Devil Trigger' from the Devil May Cry 5 soundtrack.
Gura announces that Ma, who animated the Myth Bad End, created the fully animated music video, proudly declaring them her 'dream team'.
Gura reveals the project has been 'cooking' for 'over a year. Maybe a year and a half. Or maybe two.'

highlights.topic: Good Things Come To An End
highlights.description: Gura playfully responds to a chat comment about good things ending, countering with the idea that new good things will always start.
Gura struggles with the idea of scheduling the premiere and decides she'll 'just do a live' upload, referencing a popular meme.
Gura shows a still from the music video, humorously calling it a 'Spoiler. Spoiler. Garura. Yes.'
Gura describes the song's profound emotional effect on her: 'It makes me ugly cry. Oh, this song makes me cry.'
Gura lightheartedly mentions 'quick little trauma dumping in the Discord um in the meetings, trauma dump meetings' as part of the creative process with Casey Edwards.
Gura praises Casey Edwards for taking 'the storm that was in my head and in my heart' and turning it into a piece of music she will 'cherish for the very rest of my life'.
Gura describes the song as 'a piece of my soul that I get to leave with all of you forever.'
After a humorous misdirection, Gura finally reveals the title of her new song: 'Ash.'
Gura, still flustered, humorously asks for help with the stream interface: 'Well, how do I do this again? Girl, blink twice if you need'.

chunks.summary: The VTuber, in a state of hurried excitement, directed her audience to a recently published piece of content, likely a song, which she had quickly made public without a premiere. She candidly admitted to not having time to ensure everything was perfect before publishing and expressed her inability to redirect her live stream to the new video. Apologizing for the brevity of the current stream, she explained that she was overwhelmed and unable to form coherent thoughts due to the release. She profusely thanked her viewers for their support and promised to return soon for a more detailed discussion once she had gathered her thoughts, ending the segment in a flustered but grateful state.
